checks: The three polygons are the exact integer fibers. In any combination at base 1, the endpoint coefficients are equal, so their continuous contribution is a convex mixture of K₁ and the included Minkowski midpoint. The two extreme bases retain their prescribed fibers. The support functional −z or z isolates each endpoint.

For positive planar K,L the hull of their lifts at 0 and 1 is full-dimensional and has exact middle fiber (K+L)/2. The accepted root concavity therefore bounds its maximum ordinary depth root by the average of the endpoint roots from below. Scaling both sides gives superadditivity of A^(1/2) for Minkowski sums.

Strict interior containment supplies a small disk addition K′+εB₂ within K₁. Halfspace mass at any old mark is monotone under containment, and A(B₂)>0. Combining with root superadditivity gives A(K₁)>A(K′). Any ambient cap through a middle mark has middle trace at least its ordinary own depth, including a whole-fiber pure-base trace. Two endpoint raw maxima equal to Q would thus force a middle point above Q.

If the middle is below Q, a small homothety about an interior point enlarges it and keeps the midpoint inclusion and the two endpoint fibers exact. Moving through-point thresholds at fixed base changes the nonvertical cap mass by O(t) uniformly by unit continuous normalization and the fixed common ball slab bound. The bound is independent of the integer tilt. Pure-base cuts are unchanged by the mark motion, and the homothety changes total cap areas by at most the O(t) area difference. The raw gap therefore persists uniformly on the moving middle fiber, while unchanged endpoint maxima and increasing total mass give strict normalized descent.
